subject: Continental bridge activation: US/EU/APAC traffic guidance
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: BrightTech Support <support@brighttech.com>, Jordan Lee <j.lee@paymentsco.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Continental bridge activation: US/EU/APAC traffic guidance

Hi all —

Quick update and action items while we activate the continental bridge to mitigate the partial outage in us-east-1 that is impacting token routing for some customers. We are initiating a controlled traffic crossover (US -> EU -> APAC as appropriate) to preserve low-latency routing for tenant traffic while the peering event is contained.

What we are doing now:
- Activating bridge routes and prefix announcements from EU-west and APAC-north to absorb burst traffic for affected clients.
- Enabling prefix-level KV cache warm-up for long-running sessions to reduce cold-start token costs.
- Running a small canary (5% of BrightTech traffic) through the bridge for the next 30 minutes, then ramp to 25% if no errors.

Customer-facing notes (please acknowledge):
- Expected visible effect: brief increase in observed RTT for sessions moving between continents (50–120ms delta).
- No data will be routed outside of customer-configured regions for private deployments; this affects hosted Redwood endpoints only.

Requested actions from BrightTech:
1) Please confirm whether you want us to enable the DNS low-TTL override for your endpoints (we can push a 30s override for the next 2 hours).
2) Share any sidecar IP allowlist that needs updating for EU/APAC egress.

Attachments: bridge-activation-runbook.pdf (steps + rollback), continental-routing-diagram.png (current overlay), kv-cache-snapshot-08152026.txt (diagnostic sample).

I'll post intermittent updates in this thread. Laura/Vivek — internal runbook is in the Drive link below.

Thanks,
David
David Kim
Customer Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference
(david.kim@redwood.com)

Internal notes for coordination:

David — quick ops checklist and thresholds I’m tracking:
- Rollback: automatic rollback if error rate for the canary exceeds 2.5% 5xx or latency P95 increases by >200ms sustained for 5 minutes. Manual rollback if we see stateful session failures reported by BrightTech.
- Affinity: we are preserving KV-session pointers and will wire proxy-level affinity for the canary cohort — in practice that means in-flight chat sessions should continue without re-auth. We’ll mark any exceptions in the canary logs.
- Observability: Vivek will publish a per-tenant stream of token-level errors to the BrightTech topic and open a temporary read-only Dashboard.

Marissa — please prep a short customer-facing note to describe the expected latency delta and confirmation timeframe; we’ll send once BrightTech confirms TTL override.

Running actions:
1) Vivek — enable the per-tenant read-only dashboard and push the canary config.
2) Marissa — draft the one-paragraph notification.
3) David — confirm when you push TTL override.

Laura
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 15 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Continental bridge activation: US/EU/APAC traffic guidance

BrightTech — thanks for the quick reply and confirmation.

Summary of actions taken and next steps:
- TTL override: enabled (30s) for your hosted endpoints at 10:03 PT.
- Canary: pushed 5% at 10:10 PT; observed 0.8% 5xx and P95 latency +60ms — within thresholds, ramped to 25% at 10:45 PT.
- Affinity: proxy-level session pinning was maintained for canary cohort; no re-auth required for tracked sessions.
- Dashboard: temporary read-only dashboard is live (link below) and will auto-expire after 6 hours.

Observed issues and mitigations:
- We saw a transient spike in token rehydration errors between 10:25–10:33 PT tied to an expired KV shard; Vivek rehydrated the shard and error rates dropped to baseline by 10:40 PT. Logs attached: kv-cache-snapshot-08152026.txt.
- No customer data was forwarded to unauthorized regions; all routing changes occurred within hosted topology and follow the account routing policy.

Attachments and references: bridge-activation-runbook.pdf (activated steps + rollback), continental-routing-diagram.png, Drive post-incident note: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/BRIDGE-20260815

Planned follow-up: we will produce a concise postmortem with root cause and recommended long-term mitigations by EOD Monday (2026-08-17). In the meantime, please flag any customer-visible issues in this thread — Jordan, we’re watching payment flows closely.

Thanks again for the collaboration; Laura/Marissa/Vivek — please confirm when the postmortem draft is ready for review.

-David
David Kim
